story.title: Analysis Links Climate Change to Deadly Glacier and Rock Collapse in Nepal
story.summary: Scientists have concluded that climate change significantly contributed to a recent glacier and rock collapse in Nepal, which resulted in nearly 1,400 deaths and left thousands missing. The warming climate has destabilized glaciers and thawed ground, creating conditions that led to the disaster. The combined toll from the incident now stands at 1,446 dead and at least 6,669 missing.

explore_lenses.label: What are the immediate priorities now?
explore_lenses.title: Search, shelter and a longer recovery
explore_lenses.summary: Nepal's government says rescue, relief and damage assessment are continuing, with both safe relocation and long-term rehabilitation urgent. Humanitarian agencies are also focusing on disrupted health, water, sanitation, education and child-protection services.

claims.text: As of September 17, Nepal's disaster authority reported 1,403 bodies recovered and 6,150 people missing in Nepal; combined Nepal-China totals in reporting may differ as authorities revise and reconcile cross-border counts.

Nepal's Ministry of Home Affairs says it immediately began search, rescue and emergency-relief operations, while total human and material damage was still being assessed; it calls both relocation to safety and long-term rehabilitation urgent.

UNICEF says flood damage has cut survivors off from urgent care and disrupted roads, bridges, hydropower, water, telecommunications and health facilities; it is supporting government-led assistance across health, water and sanitation, education and child protection.

Forecast: World Weather Attribution says glacier decline and permafrost degradation are expected to continue even without additional warming, and calls for stronger high-Himalaya observation, monitoring, risk communication and cross-border data sharing alongside emissions reductions and recovery support.

story_report.summary: Scientists say decades of warming helped create the conditions for a glacier and rock collapse in Nepal by destabilizing glaciers and thawing ground. The disaster has caused extensive loss of life, with reporting putting the combined Nepal-China toll at 1,446 dead and at least 6,669 missing. Nepalese authorities have begun search, rescue and emergency-relief operations as the full human and material damage continues to be assessed.

sections.heading: Flood Damage Disrupts Essential Services
sections.body: Flood damage has cut survivors off from urgent care and disrupted roads, bridges, hydropower, water systems, telecommunications and health facilities, according to UNICEF. The agency is supporting government-led assistance in health, water and sanitation, education and child protection. Nepal’s disaster authority reported on September 17 that 1,403 bodies had been recovered and 6,150 people were missing within Nepal, while cross-border totals may differ as officials revise and reconcile the figures.

sections.heading: Himalayan Risks Require Long-Term Action
sections.body: Nepal’s Home Affairs Ministry has described both relocation to safety and long-term rehabilitation as urgent while assessment of the damage continues. World Weather Attribution says glacier decline and permafrost degradation are expected to continue even without further warming. It calls for stronger observation and monitoring in the high Himalaya, clearer risk communication and cross-border data sharing, alongside emissions reductions and support for recovery.

unresolved.text: Death and missing-person figures remain provisional, and the sources reviewed do not establish the scale, timetable or financing of reconstruction.

related_stories.title: Ninth Woman Found as Ongoing Investigation Continues in South Africa
related_stories.summary: South African authorities have discovered the body of a ninth woman, all victims aged in their 20s and 30s, in a series of killings occurring on the outskirts of Johannesburg over the past two months. While police are investigating the cases, they have warned against prematurely linking all the incidents, as many women in the area express fear regarding their safety.

related_stories.title: Discovery of Nine Women's Bodies Raises Alarm Over Femicides in South Africa
related_stories.summary: The recent discovery of the bodies of nine women near Johannesburg over the past two months has alarmed South Africa, drawing attention to the ongoing issue of femicide and high violent crime rates in the country. Authorities are investigating the possibility of a serial killer or a group of killers behind these incidents.

related_stories.title: Gold Mine Collapse in Sudan Claims at Least 82 Lives
related_stories.summary: A gold mine collapse in West Kordofan, Sudan, has resulted in the deaths of at least 82 individuals, with many more injured and feared trapped under the debris. Rescue efforts are ongoing as authorities assess the situation and search for survivors.
